title: Hosted API ingress/egress fairness sandbox and enterprise SQ playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: design and run a sandboxed experiment to validate a fairness-forward approach to per‑token billing by splitting ingress (input) and egress (output/streaming) rates, with an adaptive soft-floor and grace credit system suitable for enterprise contracts and security questionnaire (SQ) commitments.

Background: Customers building bidirectional workflows (embeddings + long-form generation, retrieval-augmented generation, streaming assistants) report confusion over blended per-token bills and frequent disputes on expected vs observed spend. We need a model that is predictable for customers, defensible in enterprise SQs, and operationally simple to meter.

Hypothesis: Separately metering ingress and egress tokens, combined with an adaptive soft minimum (grace credits that scale with commit tier and recent usage variance), will reduce billing disputes by >30% and increase perceived fairness in NPS surveys for heavy streaming customers, without materially reducing revenue predictability for Redwood.

Scope:
- Design 3 pricing variants for hosted API sandbox:
  1) Split rates (ingress and egress explicit), no minimum.
  2) Split rates + soft minimum that draws on a per-customer grace credit pool (auto-refill rules configurable by commit).
  3) Split rates + adaptive floor that scales based on 30d usage volatility and allows one-hour burst forgiveness.
- Streaming semantics: charge egress at streaming-rate-per-second token rate (same as token rate but applied continuously), include handshake/keepalive accounting rules to avoid noise.
- Billing UI/Docs: add explicit ingress/egress meter breakdown in Console and monthly invoice preview for sandbox customers.
- SQ Playbook: draft responses for common auditor questions explaining directional metering, grace credit accounting, data residency and audit trails.

Experiment design:
- Duration: 6 weeks in sandbox cohorts (50 small customers, 10 mid, 5 enterprise pilot).
- Randomized assignment for small/mid; opt-in for enterprise pilot after legal signoff.
- Success metrics: billing dispute rate, invoice adjustment volume (%), customer-reported fairness (survey), delta in average revenue per active customer (ARPA) vs baseline, latency/regression risk to existing metering pipeline.

Telemetry and observability:
- Instrument ingress/egress meters, grace-credit debits/credits, dispute flags, and invoice delta events.
- Dashboards: per-customer day-level token flows, weekly dispute aggregation, and estimated monthly bill forecasting error.

Acceptance criteria:
- Billing dispute volume drops >=30% in pilot cohort OR customer NPS fairness score increases >=8 points for pilot cohort.
- No material (>0.5%) negative impact on revenue predictability in enterprise pilot.
- Console meter breakdown implemented and validated in sandbox.
- SQ playbook drafted and accepted by Security and Legal.

Out of scope: dedicated or private pricing changes, reserved capacity contract redesign, or irreversible changes to billing engine. This work will be gated and feature-flagged so we can revert to baseline metering if necessary.
metrics: billing_dispute_rate: percent of invoices with manual adjustments
customer_perceived_fairness: NPS survey question focused on pricing fairness
ARPA_delta: percent change vs baseline cohort
metering_latency_errors: count of delayed/failed meter events
acceptance_criteria: >=30% reduction in billing disputes for pilot cohort OR >=8 point increase in perceived pricing fairness NPS
Console shows ingress/egress breakdown and matches invoice preview within 0.1%
SQ playbook approved by Security/Legal and attached to pilot onboarding pack
Instrumentation captures grace credit debits with audit log entries for each event
risks_and_mitigations: Revenue volatility risk: mitigate by limiting enterprise pilot to opt-in customers and running short windowed rollouts
Metering complexity: keep billing engine changes behind feature flags and fall back to blended meter for contested invoices
Customer confusion: provide clear Console previews, email FAQs, and sample bill scenarios during onboarding
SQ backlash: involve Security and Legal early and include immutable audit trail for all grace-credit operations
